name: Matthias Mason & Co.'s Blacksmith Shop

documented_range.note: SELF-REPORTED IN THE ONLY CONTEMPORARY CHICAGO DOCUMENT THIS PROJECT HOLDS. Mason & Co. advertise as blacksmiths in the Chicago Democrat of 26 November 1833, on 'Main-street, nearly opposite Graves' Tavern'. The '& Co.' says the shop employed more than one man. The far end of the range is inferred: nothing follows the firm past 1833, and a working smithy in a town growing tenfold is far more likely to have continued than to have closed.

change_note: The building as this dataset can state it on the scene date. Where the sources give a size, a plan or a fabric, the record carries it; where they do not, the note says so attribute by attribute.

placement.position_note: THE ADDRESS IS DOCUMENTED IN A STREET NAME NOBODY ELSE USES, AND THE CROSS-REFERENCE IS WHAT PLACES IT. 'Main-street' appears nowhere in data/traces/street_control.json, the Thompson plat module or either 1834 sheet. Graves' Tavern is Dexter Graves's log tavern, which this dataset models as mansion_house at what became 84-86 Lake Street, on the NORTH side of Lake near Dearborn. 'Nearly opposite' therefore puts the smithy on the SOUTH side of Lake Street facing north across it, and 'Main-street' in November 1833 is very probably Lake Street under a colloquial name. The northing is the Lake Street south frontage band this dataset's reconstruction recipes already use; the easting is set opposite mansion_house. WHAT IS INVENTED: the exact lot, the setback and the facade bearing.
placement.symbolic_location: South Division, local ENU E 735 N -133

footprint.note: PLACEHOLDER - NO DIMENSION IS ATTESTED. 20 x 30 ft is a two-fire shop: room for two hearths, an anvil each and a horse standing in, which is what '& Co.' implies. Every number is invented.

persons.name: Matthias Mason
persons.note: HIS ADDRESS NAMES A STREET THIS PROJECT DOES NOT OTHERWISE HOLD. 'Main-street' appears nowhere in this dataset's street control, the Thompson plat module or either 1834 sheet, and it is a real 1833 Chicagoan's own word for where his shop was. The cross-reference is usable: Graves' Tavern is Dexter Graves's house, the log tavern on Lake Street that became the Mansion House at what are now 84-86 Lake Street. So 'Main-street' in November 1833 is very probably Lake Street or a stretch of it under a colloquial name. THAT IS A FINDING FOR THE STREETS LAYER, NOT A PLACEMENT, and it is recorded here rather than acted on. The Chicago Democrat of 26 November 1833 is the only contemporary Chicago document this project holds; an advertiser in it was paying to be found, which makes it strong evidence of existence and address in November 1833 and weak evidence of survival to 1 July 1835, nineteen months and about 2,400 people later.

residents.research_note: THE ADVERTISEMENT THAT CONTAINS A STREET NAME NOBODY ELSE USES, which is the most useful thing in this household and has nothing to do with its people. A blacksmith is also the trade the inferred phase will need most of: a town of 3,265 with the wagon traffic Andreas describes could not run on the two smithies this dataset models, and this record is the documented proof of a third.
